Manage and refer urgently:
If shock/SBP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.
If meningitis likely, give ceftriaxone2 2g IM. Avoid injecting > 1g IM at one injection site. If referral delayed, repeat ceftriaxone2 2g IM after 12 hours.
If fingerprick glucose < 3 (< 4 if diabetes) or ≥ 11.1 19.
If pain, give single dose paracetamol 1g orally.
FEVER

1If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely. 2If severe penicillin allergy (previous angioedema, anaphylaxis or urticaria), discuss with doctor. 3Doxycycline may interfere with oral contraceptive, advise to also use condoms. 4If also taking iron supplements or antacids, take these at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after doxycycline dose. 5If pregnant with tick bite fever, benefits of treatment with doxycycline outweigh potential risks of side effects.
• A patient with a fever has a temperature ≥ 38°C now or in the past 3 days. • If patient has been in a malaria area in past 3 months, consider malaria. 39.

Approach to the patient with a fever not needing urgent attention • If on abacavir, check for abacavir hypersensitivity reaction (AHR) 131. • If unexplained rash or lesion/s of skin/genitals/anus/rectum/mouth/eyes and ≥ 1 of: headache/backache/body pain, swollen lymph nodes, temperature > 38.5°C, fatigue, sore throat/nasal congestion/ cough, consider mpox. 40. • If sore throat, mild fever and a thick grey layer (pseudomembrane) in nose/throat that bleeds easily if touched, consider diphtheria 53. • If none of the above, or previous malaria test/s negative:
Does patient have a tick bite (small dark brown/black scab) or tick present?
Yes

Tick bite fever likely • May also have headache, body pain, rash or localised lymphadenopathy. • If tick present, grip tick close to skin using forceps and remove. • Give doxycycline3,4 100mg 12 hourly with food for 7 days. • If pregnant, give doxycycline4,5 100mg 12 hourly with food for 2 days only, then switch to azithromycin 500mg daily for 3 days. • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. • Refer if: - Unable to take medication orally - Fever persisting for > 2 days after starting treatment. • Advise to return if any of: new rash, confusion, shortness of breath, palpitations, severe weakness. Refer.
• Ask about other symptoms: assess and manage on symptom page. • If any of: headache, body pain, recent common cold, acute viral infection likely 51.

If none of above: • Check urine dipstick: if blood, leucocytes or nitrites 69. • Check for TB 102 and test for HIV 124. • Advise patient to return if other symptoms develop. • If fever recurs or persists for > 2 days and cause still uncertain, discuss/refer.
